question: In July 2025, DRDO successfully conducted two consecutive successful flight tests of the Pralay missile at which of the following locations?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam Island**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **July 2025**, the **Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO)** successfully carried out two consecutive flight tests of the **Pralay** missile.
 
• The tests were conducted from the **Integrated Test Range (ITR)** located at **Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam Island**, off the coast of **Odisha**.
 
• **Pralay** is a **surface-to-surface**, **short-range ballistic missile (SRBM)** developed for battlefield use by the **Indian Army**.
 
• The missile was tested for different ranges and demonstrated high-level accuracy by hitting the designated target with precision, meeting all mission objectives.
 
• During these flight tests, all subsystems performed satisfactorily, and the **missile's trajectory** was monitored by various **range sensors**, including **Radar**, **Electro-Optical Tracking System**, and **Telemetry** stations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Missile Specifications and Features:**
 
 
• **Pralay** is a **solid-fuel**, **quasi-ballistic** missile that has been developed to follow a path that makes it difficult for enemy **interceptor missiles** to track and destroy.
 
• It has a strike range of **150 to 500 kilometers** and can carry a payload of **350 kg to 1000 kg**.
 
• The missile is powered by a **solid-propellant rocket motor** and incorporates several new technologies, including state-of-the-art **navigation** and **integrated avionics**.
 
• It is designed to be launched from a **mobile launcher**, providing high strategic flexibility to the armed forces.
 
 
 
• **Geographic Location of the Test Site:**
 
 
• **Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam Island**, formerly known as **Wheeler Island**, is situated in the **Bay of Bengal**, approximately **10 kilometers** off the coast of **Odisha** in the **Bhadrak district**.
 
• It serves as the primary missile testing facility for India, where most of the **Agni** and **Prithvi** series missiles are flight-tested.
 
• The island was renamed in **September 2015** to honor the late Indian President and scientist, **Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam**.
 
 
 
• **Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO):**
 
 
• **DRDO** is the premier R&D organization under the **Ministry of Defence**, Government of India.
 
• It was established in **1958** by merging the Technical Development Establishment (TDEs) of the Indian Army and the Directorate of Technical Development & Production (DTDP) with the Defence Science Organisation (DSO).
 
• The organization is headquartered in **New Delhi** and works toward achieving self-reliance in critical defense technologies and systems.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Strategic Importance:** The **Pralay** missile is intended to provide India with a significant **counter-force** capability against **long-range artillery** and **tactical ballistic missiles** of adversaries.
 
• **Comparison:** Experts often compare **Pralay** to the **Russian Iskander** and **Chinese Dongfeng 12** missiles due to its ability to change its path mid-air to evade defense systems.
 
• **Other Locations Mentioned:**
 
 
• **Chandipur:** Another prominent site of the **Integrated Test Range (ITR)** in **Odisha**, typically used for testing **short-range missiles**, **rockets**, and **surface-to-air missiles** like **Akash**.
 
• **Pokhran:** Located in the **Jaisalmer** district of **Rajasthan**, it is famous as the site for India’s **nuclear tests** (1974 and 1998) and is also used for testing **artillery guns** and **tanks**.
 
• **Balasore:** The district in **Odisha** that houses the **Integrated Test Range** facilities at **Chandipur**.
 
 
 
• **Technology:** The **Pralay** missile uses a **canister-based** launch system, which allows for faster deployment and longer shelf-life by protecting the missile from environmental degradation.
